title: Context splits: even the streakiest scorers barely move
headline_insight: Of the 50 highest-minute players, the most context-sensitive shooter is Payton Pritchard, whose True Shooting % swings by only about 4.4 points on average across defense tier, venue, and rest -- his biggest single split is +6.0 TS points on the second night of a back-to-back.
what_it_means: Each player's efficiency is sliced three ways -- top-10 vs bottom-10 defenses, home vs away, and back-to-back vs rested -- to see whose shooting is most schedule-dependent. The headline is how little moves: the single most context-sensitive of the league's workhorses averages a ~4-point TS swing, and most of the top 50 sit lower. Player efficiency is far stickier across context than the 'he's a road warrior / he feasts on tired legs' narratives suggest.
how_to_read: context_sensitivity_score is the mean absolute TS% gap across the three dimensions; the per-dimension delta_ts_pct fields show which split drives it.
why_it_matters: It sets an honest expectation for how much a matchup or rest situation should nudge a player projection -- for most stars, only slightly.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY: cells below 10 player-games are dropped as insufficient, first games of a team-season have unknown rest, and no opponent/lineup adjustment is applied -- raw split dispersion only, not a causal or edge claim.
